name: SF Economic Justice Center (formerly Financial Justice Project)
description: Helps reduce or eliminate certain city fines and fees (parking, towing, etc.) for eligible residents
fullDescription: The San Francisco Treasurer's Economic Justice Center (which now houses the Financial Justice Project's work) helps low-income residents and people experiencing homelessness lower city fines and fees, and offers free financial counseling.
whatTheyOffer:
- Online tool to find discounts on city fines, fees, and tickets
- Discounts for towing and booting, public transit, tickets, and utilities
- Help with legal and court debt, ambulance bills, and animal care fees
- Free 1-on-1 financial counseling
- Advocacy to reform fines and fees that hurt low-income communities
howToGetIt:
1. Visit the Fine & Fee Discounts page on the Economic Justice Center website
2. Filter by the type of fine or fee you need help with
3. Review the discounts you may qualify for and follow the steps to claim them
4. Many low-income San Franciscans qualify for 50% or more off
5. Questions: email economic.justice@sfgov.org or call 415-701-2311
address: 1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place, San Francisco, CA 94102
keywords: Financial Justice Project, Economic Justice Center, SF Treasurer, fine and fee discounts, parking ticket, towing fee, booting fee, court fines, ambulance bill, fee reduction, low-income, San Francisco, SFMTA, financial counseling
